items.quote: We were declared the successful resolution applicant for GVK Energy Limited under the CIRP process. This marks our entry into hydro generation through the operational 330 -megawatt Alaknanda plant in Uttarakhand.

items.statement: Signed shareholders' agreement with Druk Green Power for 770 MW hydropower project in Bhutan via 49:51 JV
items.quote: We signed a shareholders' agreement with Druk Green Power, our project partner, for a 770-megawatt hydropower project. The project will be developed through a 49:51 joint venture.

items.statement: India power demand rose 11.5% YoY to 502 billion units in Q2, coal/lignite supplied 73% of incremental generation
items.quote: India's power demand rose 11.5% year -on-year to 502 billion units in Quarter 2 with lower hydropower output because of weak monsoon s. Coal and lignite stepped up supply 73% of incremental generation needed to meet the demand.

items.statement: Adani Power sales volume grew 11.5% to 26.4 billion units in Q2 FY27, PLF improved to 70.1%
items.quote: Consolidated sales volume expanded by 11.5% to 26.4 billion units in Quarter 2 FY27, compared to 23.7 billion units in Quarter 2 of last year.

items.statement: Continuing EBITDA rose 18% to INR6,321 crores in Q2 FY27, H1 FY27 continuing EBITDA grew 20.1% to INR13,304 crores
items.quote: Our continuing EBITDA for the quarter for FY27 was INR6,321 crores, compared to INR5,333 crores in quarter 2 of last year. H1 FY27 continuing EBITDA grew by 20.1% to INR13,304 crores.

items.statement: PPA realization improved 12.7% on continuing basis, supported by pass-through of import coal indices and recent medium-term PPAs
items.quote: PPA realization improved by 12.7% on a continuing basis, supported by the pass-through of import coal indices and recent medium-term PPAs.

items.statement: Imported coal landed cost increased ~50% YoY, fuel cost rose 41.8% to INR10,229 crores in Q2 FY27
items.quote: This rise was driven by increased volume s, coupled with an approximate 50% increase in the landed cost of imported coal.

items.statement: Gujarat PPA tariff linked to index, imported fuel cost increase reflects after 6+ months, likely in Q3 FY27
items.quote: Therefore, it will not get reflected even in next quarter because the indexing mechanism is such that whatever fuel prices has remained in this quarter will not get reflected in next two quarters. Probably it will get reflected in the third quarter.

items.statement: Bangladesh PPA tariff determined on international prices, immediately reflects fuel cost changes
items.quote: In case of Bangladesh PPA, it has positive impact because the Bangladesh tariff is determined based on international prices. So whenever international price goes up, it will immediately get reflected in their billing.

items.statement: Received ~INR6,000 crores from GUVNL in H1 FY27, contributed to internal accruals and liquidity
items.quote: you will notice that we have received a significant amount from GUVNL, which is nearly about INR6,000 crores. This has also contributed to our internal accruals.

items.statement: Total debt INR61,860 crores as of Sep 30, 2026 vs INR53,556 crores Mar 31, 2026; net debt flat at ~INR45,000 crores
items.quote: As of September 30, 2026, total debt stood at INR61,860 crores, compared to INR53,556 crores as of March '26. Net debt stood at INR45,846 crores as of September 30, 2026, compared to INR45,022 crores as of March 31, '26.

items.statement: Finance costs decreased 9.7% to INR760 crores in Q2 FY27 despite higher gross debt, due to disciplined liquidity management
items.quote: Finance costs for the quarter decreased by 9.7% to INR760 crores in compared to INR842 crores in Q2 of last year, driven by disciplined debt and liquidity management.

items.statement: Expect interest costs to remain largely flat despite rising market rates, aided by credit rating upgrade to AA+
items.quote: As a result of the improvement in our credit rating and all these things, we are expecting our interest cost and financing costs to remain largely flat.

items.statement: Nuclear power draft rules circulated, stakeholder comments process completed, rules expected to be notified soon
items.quote: the draft rules and regulation have been circulated for the comments and the process of taking comments from the stakeholders has been over, and we expect that the rules and regulation will be notified soon.

items.statement: Normal thermal PLF expectation ~65%, Q2 FY27 PLF 70.1% due to low hydro, H1 FY27 average PLF 74%
items.quote: The normal expectation of our thermal projects is to operate at a PLF of around 65%. Due to the lower hydro generation availability during this quarter, our PLF has been higher than norm al. the PLF for the current quarter was around 70%.While the half yearly is, approximately 74%.

items.statement: Reversed INR19.7 billion alternate coal compensation claims from Haryana DISCOM due to unresolved disputes, conservative accounting per auditor advice
items.quote: This relates to the claims which we have raised regarding domestic coal shortfall. Tthere are certain issues starting from 2021 to '23 and onwards, and discussions are ongoing. So we have reversed that at this stage to adopt conservative accounting principles for the time being.

items.statement: No change in Jaiprakash assets minority stake status, will inform market when evaluated
items.quote: At this moment, there is no change. As and when we willevaluate it, we'll inform the market. No change in status as of now.

items.statement: Expects ~700 crore incremental EBITDA from 2.5 bps MDR on current GMV of 28 lakh crore; FY28 estimate of ~900 crore considered ballpark
items.quote: on our GMV, which is 28 lakh crores, at a current scale, 2.5 bps would give you something slightly more than 700 crores. So if you're looking at FY28 numbers, that sounds ballpark, right.

items.statement: Revenue growth sustained at 28% for two quarters; excluding PIDF, growth is in the 30s
items.quote: we have now seen two consistent quarters of 28% growth. And while we stick by the reported numbers, if you exclude PIDF from the previous year's same quarters, this number is in the 30s.

items.statement: Device capex expected to remain ~400 crore per half-year on an inward device count basis
items.quote: On capex, yes, we have said it was about 400 crores on a kind of inward devices count basis, and we expect that to be the same.

items.statement: Net payment margin improved to 9 bps from 8.5 bps due to pricing discipline and mix shift toward higher-margin products like EMI, DCC, enterprise
items.quote: I think part of it is a little bit higher. We have a certain threshold, certain type of merchants; what type of pricing do we want to make? So I think there's just a little bit of additional discipline around that number, which we have imposed.

items.statement: Consumer market share is a primary KPI; committed to aggressive acquisition via product and partnerships, not just marketing spend
items.quote: Consumer market share is ours to win. And I remain committed. And I'm surprised that we unlocked some shocking, surprising things that were restricting our growth. And they were not just internal. They were external, if you will. And I'm very happy to say this, that we are going to go all in on market share.

items.statement: Shifted consumer loan distribution to pure distribution model without DLG or risk-reward bonuses; volumes and revenue pleasantly surprised
items.quote: we switched our business model completely towards distribution without requiring any upside off or any DLG to be given in consumer business. And I think that has shown us the result. We've been able to distribute a large amount of credit to the small or large consumer demands.

items.statement: Device deployments ~700,000 in Q2; focus on high-quality, high-potential merchants for financial services cross-sell
items.quote: Good to see another good quarter: 700,000-odd devices rolled out in the quarter.

items.statement: Postpaid disbursements scaling faster than first launch; ~9,000 crore quarterly run-rate target; 10 million customer base; EBITDA positive
items.quote: In one or two years, I don't know whether it will be a dash amount of quarters or a dash dash amount of quarters, but it has a target expectation of those numbers. There is no secret about it. Why would we not want to reach those numbers?

items.statement: Board approved enabling resolution to invest up to 500 crore in Paytm Cloud Technologies over 12 months for potential seed investments in international markets and subsidiary needs
items.quote: we took an enabling resolution that we can put up to 500 crores in the subsidiary. The same 500 crores, up to that number, can be put in one of our international subsidiaries as well. And to the extent that we, and this is allowed over 12 months in multiple tranches, right?

items.statement: Willing to lose large enterprise merchants demanding negative contribution margins; contract with large insurance company expired and not renewed at loss-making pricing
items.quote: We have been very meticulous about being disciplined around this number. There have been two or three customers that have been affected because of that, and we are perfectly happy to let them go to competition.

items.statement: MDR on UPI timing depends on NPCI decision; Paytm and industry are operationally ready to implement immediately post-Diwali
items.quote: Industry plays a bigger role. We are one of the participants. We are ready. We can do it. We do it. We already make MDR base revenue, credit card on UPI, UPI credit line, which is postpaid; issuing, acquiring - everything is working. It works

items.statement: DLG mix is not actively managed; accept DLG if lenders require it as it is revenue- and profitability-accretive by unlocking more merchant lending volume
items.quote: We don't say no to a lender just because they want DLG. We don't route more to a lender who has less DLG or no DLG. The idea is to find the right lender for the borrower and to do as much business as possible.

items.statement: Travel and wealth (including gold) businesses face headwinds; equity broking doing well on MTF but overall market volumes soft
items.quote: Travel has been a little bit sort of on and off. So there are headwinds in the travel industry as well. And there's been a little bit of headwind overall in wealth, including the gold business.

items.statement: Merchant loan business continues strong with TAM expansion on both smaller and larger ticket sizes
items.quote: The merchant loan business continues to do very well, including some TAM expansion opportunities that we have talked about, both on the slightly smaller ticket size, as well as the larger ticket size, around the whole business that we have been doing for the last seven years.

items.statement: Platform fees (subscription + transaction share) being tested with Meta/Google for AI services to small merchants; monetization expected within a year
items.quote: We are working with Meta and Google, actually rather Meta, where we are charging a monthly platform fee. And then we get some percentage of spend also. So all these models are showing up.

items.statement: Net payment margin improved from 8.5 to 9 basis points after a large negative contribution margin customer contract ended.
items.quote: the evidence of that is in the point that Vijit was mentioning, that eight and a half has gone to nine, which is the net payment margin number.

items.statement: A materially large negative contribution margin customer contract finished and will not be renewed if it requires negative contribution.
items.quote: this was a materially large, negative contribution margin customer. Our contract finished, and we will not do it if a negative contribution is taken.

items.statement: PCTL approved an enabling resolution for up to Rs 500 crores over 12 months to fund overseas ventures including UAE and Luxembourg subsidiaries.
items.quote: So that's the plan, but we don't have a firm number on it, which is why we have taken an enabling up to Rs 500 crores, and we have taken it for up to twelve months so that we don't have to keep kind of going back to the board for the same type of approval.

items.statement: AI platform monetization for merchants will be recorded under the marketing services revenue line.
items.quote: So of the three revenue lines, it will come in marketing services, of course the nature of that will evolve over time, but the vast majority, if not all of this, will be in marketing services.

items.statement: A large lender paused DLG for six quarters but will resume next quarter; management is indifferent to DLG and prioritizes long-term lending partnerships over DLG negotiations.
items.quote: What was meant to be maybe a temporary pause ended up being six quarters, right? So it's not a huge surprise to us that at some point they would want DLGs again. Like I said, we're largely indifferent, so we don't like to challenge them on all the details of it.

items.statement: EBITDA will continue to expand in absolute terms next quarter despite the DLG drag on contribution margin.
items.quote: We do think EBITDA will continue to go up next quarter despite this drag.

items.statement: Capex increased in the first half; depreciation will rise in FY28 due to lag, but investments target higher engagement, retention, and financial services revenue with strong payback.
items.quote: with the lag in FY28 and so on, there will be more depreciation, but it is all being done for a specific purpose, which is higher engagement, higher retention, higher financial services revenue.

items.statement: Monthly transacting users added 5 million this quarter versus a historical 1-2 million per quarter; target is one-third market share in consumer business.
items.quote: by the way, we hit internally even 100 million sometimes, even the users on our platform. So I'm going to say that our target is to take one-third market share in this business.

items.statement: Sales team additions are significant but take time to mature; new hires start with retention and revisit roles before deployment to drive Soundbox merchant additions.
items.quote: they take time to get mature. We sort of train them, and we first give them retention jobs, revisits in the markets, if you will, and then we give them deployment jobs.

items.statement: Management estimates upwards of 10 million of the 16 million net active device merchants are good-quality and creditworthy based on aging and GMV thresholds.
items.quote: I personally see on a base of 16 million, we believe that upwards of 10 million are definitely good-quality merchants.

items.statement: UPI MDR framework of 2.5 bps is not yet implemented; management has haircut the estimate for various scenarios and expects clarity in Q2-Q3 after implementation.
items.quote: I think what we have put forward is a number that we are confident of delivering. And like Vijay said in the response to an earlier question, that there are certain scenarios under which, hopefully, we'll do better than this; we obviously, when we're putting out a number, we don't put the high end of our number; we put, you know, we sort of haircut it for various scenarios.

items.statement: NPCI postponed UPI MDR implementation by a few days before October 15 go-live; management believes framework is final and unlikely to change.
items.quote: it was postponed maybe a few days, maybe a couple of days, before the implementation go live. So our understanding is, whatever those things are all sorted out, had they not postponed it, keeping in mind Diwali and the festive season coming up, then it would have gone live on October 15th in the format that they have put out there.

items.statement: Indirect expenses (including marketing, sales, service, cloud) should grow at less than half the rate of contribution margin growth over a 3-4 quarter period to achieve structural operating leverage.
items.value: less than half of revenue growth
items.quote: our indirect expenses, including higher expenses in marketing and sales and service and cloud expenses, et cetera, should over a three to four quarter period, grow at less than half of revenue growth, right? Revenue growth slash CM growth.

items.statement: Lending growth relies on cautious underwriting and conservative accounting; management avoids loosening policies to prevent future credit cycles from setting back the business many quarters.
items.quote: We don't count on, hey, we are going to be reckless and loosen the policies and those sorts of things. And there's a reason why we want to be very cautious and very responsible about this because now we have over a dozen lending partners.

items.statement: Consumer UPI market share is low due to external network alignment issues, but product and technology improvements are driving confidence to win share; merchant side is already winning.
items.quote: consumer businesses are ours to win. There have been, I would say, non-internal, not just led by us, issues that have made us have so little UPI market share on the consumer side, if you will. Our product and capabilities are continuously moving up.

items.statement: Eligible GMV mix for MDR is not changing dramatically; small merchant business growing very fast, online business growing fast post-embargo, enterprise improving via EMI and DCC offerings.
items.quote: I think the mix is not changing dramatically because obviously where Paytm has unique strengths is in the small merchant business, which is growing very, very fast. And for different reasons of enterprise business and the online business is also growing quite fast, right?

items.statement: PCTL serves as the investment vehicle for foreign ventures including UAE business setup and Luxembourg subsidiary; One97 Singapore handles legacy marketing cloud business for telecom/enterprises.
items.quote: PCTL is an entity through which we make investments in some foreign ventures. So, for example, we had announced the setting up of a business in the UAE. We have announced the subsidiary in Luxembourg. So a lot of that is done through PCTL.

items.statement: FY27 revenue expected to remain soft and trail FY26 levels; EBITDA margin guided at 25-30% for FY27 with scope for improvement in Q4
items.quote: To sum up, we expect FY27 revenue will remain soft and to trail last year's levels. This reflects cautious client spending amid global macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guided at 25-30% for FY27 with scope for improvement in Q4 as recent wins ramp up
items.quote: Hence, we expect the EBITDA margin to remain in our guided range of 25% to 30% for FY27 ,with a scope for improvement in Q4 as the recent wins ramp up.

items.statement: Cautious client spending and discretionary spend under scrutiny; clients were in wait-and-watch mode on AI until September
items.quote: Across the industry, client s remain selective and discretionary spending is still under scrutiny. Our Q2 performance reflects that, along with the ramp-down at a couple of our large enterprise clients.

items.statement: Clients now asking for AI-enabled solutions; conversations shifted from headcount to business outcomes
items.quote: Today, almost every conversation includes agentic AI, or it starts with agentic AI, I can say. Clients are asking for Odoo with a gentic AI, or you can reverse it, agentic AI with Odoo, a gentic AI with Salesforce, agentic AI with data engineering.

items.statement: Q2 EBITDA margin 25.7% down from 30.3% QoQ and 30.4% YoY due to revenue decline; cost optimization and AI productivity improvements offset some impact
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 9.7 crores with a margin of 25.7% compared to 30.3% in the last quarter and 30.4% in Q2 FY26. The moderation in margin was primarily attributable to lower revenue, offset by cost optimization and AI-led productivity improvements.

items.statement: Secured strategic wins in banking (South America, UK, Europe), global ports, and education (Australia); three of Q2 wins in banking
items.quote: During the quarter, we secured market wins across diversified sectors , and our key technology offerings include banking in South America, banking in the U.K., banking in Europe, global ports, and education industry in Australia. Three of our Q2 wins are in banking.

items.statement: One large enterprise client that reduced team due to AI testing is now scaling back up with AI requirement
items.quote: Yes. That's one of the clients that have started scaling back, and we can see more revenue from that client, given what was earlier because they were testing with AI and all.

items.statement: 80% revenue from overseas; North America 59%, India 20%, Europe 6%, Australia 4%, Rest of World 11%; no constant currency reporting
items.quote: Our geographical mix remained diversified, with 80% of revenue coming from overseas markets. North America contributed 59% of total revenue, followed by India at 20%, Europe at 6%, Australia at 4%, and the rest of the world at 11%.

items.statement: Focus on disciplined working capital management and cash conversion; cash and bank balance INR 17.6 crores as of Sep 30, 2026
items.quote: Our focus remains on disciplined working capital management and cash conversion. The Board has also declared a second interim dividend of INR 1 per share, taking our total interim dividend for H1 to INR 5 per share, which is about 72% of our H1 profit after tax.

items.statement: Debt-free balance sheet maintained
items.quote: On cash and balance sheet, we continue to remain a debt -free balance sheet, maintain a debt -free balance sheet with a cash and bank balance of INR 17.6 crores as of 30th September 2026.

items.statement: Second interim dividend of INR 1 per share declared; total H1 interim dividend INR 5 per share (~72% of H1 PAT); shareholder returns remain priority
items.quote: The Board has also declared a second interim dividend of INR 1 per share, taking our total interim dividend for H1 to INR 5 per share, which is about 72% of our H1 profit after tax. This reflects our continued commitment to shareholder returns while keeping a strong cash position.

items.statement: Headcount reduced ~10% from 550 to ~495; rationalization plus attrition; AI enabling 2-3x productivity per engineer; minimal hiring vs last year
items.quote: You can say adjustment plus a few resources they left because they got other opportunity. And we were able to manage those losses with the help of AI. So , this year, even we have not done recruitment, I can say compared to last year, 5%- 10% maximum. And our productivity is same. Still, we have people to deliver more work. So this AI has helped us to increase the output drastically. One person is

items.statement: Opened sales office in Australia for local contracts and bidding; team based in India
items.quote: So in Australia, we have opened a sales office, particularly for local client contracts and bidding purposes. Employees' complete team is based out in India only. So we have just recently established that office, and we expect in coming few months or few quarters that we'll get some business.

items.statement: Revenue per employee and utilization key focus for H2; AI deployment to raise output per person before adding hires
items.quote: A key priority for H2 is to drive higher utilization and revenue per employee by deploying our engineers across platforms, using AI to raise output per person, and filling capacity from our existing team before adding new hires.

items.statement: FY27 revenue softness dependent on geopolitical stability; 20% growth target for FY28 conditional on no geopolitical problems
items.quote: Now if you will ask a question about the next year, I'm very optimistic that we will do this .But again, condition is that geopolitical problem, all these things should not be there.

items.statement: Client concentration risk acknowledged; pipeline not deep enough to offset large client ramp-downs in Q2; building stronger pipeline
items.quote: When these accounts slowed, our pipeline was not deep enough to fully offset the impact within the quarter. We are now building a pipeline, even a strong pipeline enough that no client-specific decision can move our quarter the way this one did.

items.statement: Clients initially explored in-house AI but realized need for human experts to control/validate AI; now outsourcing with AI requirement
items.quote: Initially, a few customers, I can say, they tried. Not sure maybe they were excited to know about the AI or maybe they were exploring. They have done some jobs on their side. But now what they have started that they have started outsourcing the projects, adding features , and they are focusing mainly on the business side.

items.statement: Upgraded to Frappe Bronze Partner in India; Select Partner for both Anthropic (Claude) and OpenAI networks
items.quote: Alongside our Anthropic and OpenAI select partnerships, we have been upgraded to Frappe Bronze Partner in India.

items.statement: Exploring cybersecurity vertical as AI needs guardrails; still in exploration phase
items.quote: For cybersecurity, we are still exploring. So we will update what we are planning or what we are going to do in cybersecurity. But definitely, we are exploring cybersecurity because AI need guardrails.

items.statement: Building agentic AI platforms for banking (compliance, transaction monitoring, fraud detection), telecom (low-code/no-code agent platform), US client (legacy migration via 8 agents), and marketing intelligence
items.quote: For them, we are building a complete agentic AI platform, which will be used for intelligent assistance to customers, to the banks operation staff, and to their leadership. We are in discussion with them to also build, you can say, a compliance and transaction monitoring system, which means for fraud detection, anti-money laundering, all of that, all AI-based agents.

items.statement: Management does not provide forward-looking revenue or EBITDA forecasts but sees sustained growth momentum and healthy order pipeline
items.quote: We don't give the forecasting and the you know I would say forward looking numbers but what we are seeing in the market today is there is a sustained growth momentum for us.

items.statement: Sustained growth momentum with healthy order pipeline and demand across all industry segments except healthcare compliance
items.quote: We continue to have a good healthy order pipeline and healthy demand. So hiring continues, our you know AI training continues, our relationship, our projects continues.

items.statement: EBITDA margin returned to 24% steady state; PAT margin improved to 16% QoQ; management targets 24% EBITDA and 14-15% PAT margins
items.quote: EBITDA margin comes back to the steady state number, last quarter it was 23, this quarter it is 24 percent, so we have good growth here. PAT margins have improved from 14 percent to 16 percent Q-Q from 22 to 26 crores.

items.statement: Seven consecutive quarters of over 6% sequential operating revenue growth indicating sustained momentum
items.quote: One important factor is seven quarters of sequential operating revenue growth of 6 percent, over 6 percent quarter on quarter for last seven quarters.

items.statement: No pricing pressure observed; revenue growth outpaces headcount growth; profit increases despite outcome-based pricing discussions
items.quote: So there is no such pricing pressure that we see right now. I think what is more important to the customer is how much value are we adding using AI, without AI, whichever way we go, the customer is trusting us, banking on us to provide solutions to solve their business problems.

items.statement: Over 90% of revenue from existing clients; average relationship age over 9 years; 50 large enterprise clients including Fortune 500 and Fortune 100
items.quote: Typically every year we have more than 90% business coming from the existing clients. The remaining business comes from the new clients.

items.statement: Revenue mix: USA 49%, Europe 40%, UAE 8%, Rest of World 3%; Europe provides counterbalance to US macro challenges
items.quote: USA is now at 49%, Europe is at 40% which is a good counterbalance to the challenging macro environment posed by the Trump government, UAE at 8% which is kind of a steady state, rest of the world including India is about 3%.

items.statement: Net addition of 43 employees in Q2 on base of 1,800+; net hiring range 10-15% for year; revenue growth not mapping to headcount due to AI efficiency
items.quote: The net number if I were to tell you is about 43 net addition that we added in this quarter, on a base of 1800 plus, this is like about what you say 10, much like 2, 3, how much it is, actually 3, 4%.

items.statement: Trade receivables increased due to some clients extending payment terms from 60 to 90 days and payment delays; provisions made; confident of collection
items.quote: Some pressure of the you know client ends where and then some of the clients actually change their terms also. So from 60 days to 90 days and some of the clients have been delaying their payments but these are long standing clients so we know that it is not a risk.

items.statement: Actively scouting M&A targets: ServiceNow or AI/data companies with $5-15M revenue, overseas customers, India delivery; good lead flow in recent months
items.quote: We are actively looking at ServiceNow companies or AI and data companies in a 5 to 15 million dollar revenue range with overseas customers and delivery in India. So this is the kind of ﬁlter that we have applied and any deal that comes to us through any banker has to meet this ﬁlter before it even gets there

items.statement: Not a dividend yield company; prefers reinvesting cash for growth via AI and sales; buybacks and dividends only when needed
items.quote: We are not a company that you should look at for dividend yields. We pay dividends, we do buybacks as and when needed, but it is not an active strategy for us to give the cash back to the Investor, we would rather use it to build the business and navigate the challenging times that is posed ahead of us by investing in AI and you know being more aggressive on the sales side.

items.statement: Offshore-heavy model with <50 people across US, Europe, Middle East out of ~1,900 total; not visa-dependent; H1B restrictions do not affect business
items.quote: even if you look at today, out of this, you know, almost 1,900 people team, you would have less than 50 people across all the three geographies, which is very insigniﬁcant in the entire equation. And therefore, you know, there was this H1B restriction four, ﬁve years ago. And here, you know, it is made extremely tough by the Trump government, but it doesn't really affect us because we are not a vi

items.statement: USD revenue grew 22% YoY and 6% QoQ; constant currency growth 22% YoY
items.quote: On the USD terms, we have grown 22% Y-o-Y, remaining was INR appreciation. The dollar appreciation against INR. On the quarterly basis also, I am happy to announce that we have grown at 6% Q-o-Q, which is quite a good growth in the current market situation.

items.statement: Macro environment and visa norms not negatively affecting business due to offshore model and client relationships; healthcare compliance segment shows worry signs
items.quote: I don't think these macro factors are negatively affecting us. The third point that we talked about was the visa. So we are not, I mean, from day one we have not been dependent on H1B visas, we have always been offshore heavy and bulk of our revenue is through our delivery centres, delivered through our delivery centres across India.

items.statement: Director loan of up to $1M to Mitesh Bohra (employee and director of InfoBeans Inc) repaid in 3-4 months with interest per company policy
items.quote: We have a policy in the US where the employees can get a loan of up to 1 million dollar and since Mitesh is also a director and an employee of InfoBeans INC, so, he availed that facility and it was a, I would say, 3-4 month period between which it was repaid as well.

items.statement: Guides 5-7% quarterly AUM growth going forward
items.quote: We continue to guide for a 5% to 7% growth on a quarterly basis from here on.

items.statement: Guides 25 bps Opex reduction for FY27
items.quote: We continue to guide for a 25 basis reduction in Opex for FY '27.

items.statement: Expects credit cost to stabilize or reduce from current 1.37%
items.quote: We are at 1.37% now, we should stabilize here or possibly reduce unless something drastically changes in the environment.

items.statement: Expects to hold ROA around 4.5-4.6% over short period
items.quote: Over a short period, we think we should be able to hold on to this.

items.statement: AUM at INR 12,592 crores, up 6% Q-o-Q and 27% Y-o-Y
items.quote: Overall, our AUM stood at INR 12,592 crores, up 6% Q-o-Q and 27% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: MSME AUM at INR 9,669 crores, up 18% Y-o-Y and 4.3% Q-o-Q
items.quote: Our MSME AUM is at INR 9,669 crores, which is 77% of our AUM with a growth of 18% on a Y-o-Y basis and 4.3% on a Q-o-Q basis.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM at INR 2,906 crores, 23% of total AUM
items.quote: The loan against gold AUM is at INR 2,906 crores.

items.statement: MSME disbursements grew 6% Q-o-Q to INR 855 crores
items.quote: MSME disbursements grew 6% in the quarter to INR 855 crores.

items.statement: Raised PLR by 25 bps in October to pass on higher borrowing costs
items.quote: Yes. So we did a PLR increase of 25 basis points this month.

items.statement: Added 1 branch in Q2, 6 branches in H1; total branches 257
items.quote: We upfronted the branch expansion in H2 of FY '26 and therefore, we have only added 1 branch during the quarter and 6 branches in the half year, bringing the total branch count to 257 as on September 2026.

items.statement: Gold loans adding ~INR 40 lakhs net growth per branch per month
items.value: INR 40 lakhs per branch per month
items.quote: Each branch is adding approximately INR 40 lakhs a month in net growth, that's roughly INR 1.2 crores per branch per quarter.

items.statement: Competitive intensity in gold loans rising; pricing rationalization likely
items.quote: Competitive intensity in gold is rising and some pricing rationalization is likely.

items.statement: GNPA at 2.64%, down 2 bps Q-o-Q and 13 bps Y-o-Y; PCR at 42.24%

items.quote: Yes, we capitalize costs that are directly attributable to it. It is still work in progress. Kairos is not yet fully capitalized as a platform, but there are some costs which we need to capitalize.

items.statement: Absorbed first phase of annual wage increments in Q2 (frontline/mid-level); senior increments in Q3; margin expanded despite wage hikes and onboarding 3,000 people ahead of revenue
items.quote: One of the things to also bear in mind is this quarter, we've expanded margins despite absorbing the first phase of annual wage increments as well and the cost of onboarding 3,000 people largely ahead of revenue coming in as well.

items.statement: >50% of revenue non-linear (outcome-based, platform-led, value-linked); objective to increase share of non-linear revenue over time
items.quote: Today, more than 50% of our revenues are already non-linear in nature, which we understand is an industry-leading metric. As we continue to productize our capabilities, our objective is to further increase the share of non-linear, outcome-based, platform-led, and value-linked revenues over time.

items.statement: BFS vertical grew 19% YoY and 9% QoQ in constant currency; added 9 new logos; broad-based growth driven by consumer debt servicing and cost pressure
items.quote: In Q2 FY27, our BFS vertical grew 19% year-on-year and 9% sequentially in constant currency terms. We added nine new logos during the quarter.

items.statement: CMT vertical grew 6% YoY, flat QoQ in constant currency; 2 new logos; volatility from timing of work packets and program transitions in consumer tech portfolio
items.quote: Coming to the CMT vertical, revenues grew 6% year-on-year and were flat sequentially in constant currency terms with two new logos added during the quarter.

items.statement: Diverse portfolio (utilities & retail) grew 25% YoY, flat QoQ in constant currency; 2 new logos; utilities focused on cost optimization and nearshore delivery
items.quote: And finally, our diverse portfolio, comprising of our utilities and our retail business grew 25% year-on-year and was flat sequentially in constant currency terms with two new logos added during the quarter.

items.statement: Hedge book: GBP 69.2M coverage for next 12 months at avg INR 116.6/GBP; USD 68.5M coverage at avg INR 95.7/USD
items.quote: As on 30th September 2026, our hedge book, we have coverage of GBP69.2 million for the next 12 months with an average rate of INR 116.6 per pound and coverage of USD68.5 million with an average rate of INR95.7 per dollar.

items.statement: Normalized DSO 67-69 days; FCF to PAT 150% for Q2, 126% for H1
items.quote: Normalized DSO continued to be in the range of 67 to 69 days. Our FCF to PAT for the quarter was 150% and for the half year it was 126%.

items.statement: Cash and bank balance INR 4.1B; net debt INR 15.3B vs INR 17.1B end of June 2026
items.quote: Turning to the balance sheet, our cash and bank balance stood at INR4.1 billion and net debt was INR15.3 billion versus INR17.1 billion at the end of June 2026.

items.statement: H1 effective tax rate 23.2%; FY27 expected effective tax rate 22%-24%
items.quote: Our tax rate for the first half was 23.2%. For FY27, we expect our effective tax rate to be between 22% and 24%.

items.statement: Expect H2 FY27 stronger than H1; raised lower end of revenue guidance based on large deal ramps, banking client transition, 17 new logos, healthy pipeline
items.quote: If you recall, even in our commentary at the end of the first quarter as well, we had stated right then as well that we expect H2 to be stronger than H1, and if you think about how Q2 has played out and what we have seen across the board, if nothing else, it has only reaffirmed our confidence on how the second half of the year is going to play out.

items.statement: Medium-term margin target 14%-15% EBIT; expect 50-75 bps annual improvement over next 2-3 years from right-shoring, automation, process excellence, non-linear pricing, portfolio quality
items.quote: We do expect that 50 to 75 basis point improvement to continue to play out over the next couple of years as well, while we remain focused on the 14% to 15% band. Where is that going to come from? I think right-shoring will play a role, automation will play a role, process excellence will play a role, operating parameters, account-level margin improvements, reducing dependence on low margin and los

items.statement: See AI-native startups emerging; partnering with them for speed-to-market and tech; one large deal won via AI-startup referral; lines blurring between tech and operations
items.quote: Yes, so I think, Girish, there is an opportunity out here where we can coexist with these folks. The way to think about a lot of the AI-native start-ups is oftentimes they may have a technology that has got relevance but may not have the domain depth. What we lead with is the depth and vertical domain.

items.statement: M&A philosophy consistent: plug capability gaps (e.g., QBSS for revenue cycle, TeleMedik for Puerto Rico footprint/clinical ops) or distribution access; not aggressive for assets sake
items.quote: There are 2 things that we're really looking at, number one, it has to be something which plugs a capability gap. For instance, it could be in healthcare, it could be something that could be in -- we did something on the retail side 2 years back when we acquired Ascensos as an example or it could be something on the distribution access side.

items.statement: Healthcare payer program scope recalibration after CMS rate adjustments caused timing challenges; transformative payer BPaaS engagement wind-down largely behind
items.quote: While it grew 5% year-on-year in Q2 and 11% in Q1, one of the things that you have seen is also the fact that we talked about the fact that there was a timing challenge with some of the payer program as Medicare Advantage clients recalibrated scope after some o f the CMS rate adjustments

items.statement: Exceptional charge from Q1 related to two clients; relationships remain strong, actively engaged on recovery, optimistic on outcome
items.quote: Let me also give you a quick update on the exceptional charge item we recognized last quarter relating to our two clients. Our relationships with both clients remain strong. We are actively engaged with them on recovery and we remain optimistic about the outcome.

name: Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Limited

items.statement: Aspire to grow fresh business at 20%+ consistently for a long period and hope to maintain that for this year
items.quote: So as a company, we aspire to grow at 20% plus on fresh business consistently for a long period of time. We hope to maintain that for this year as well.

items.statement: GST exemption demonstrated how affordability unlocks demand for retail health insurance, particularly among first-time buyers
items.quote: The GST exemption demonstrated how strongly affordability unlocks demand for retail health insurance, particularly amongst the first-time buyers.

items.statement: Underwriting result for Q2 FY27 was Rs. 99 crore vs loss of Rs. 40 crore in Q2 FY26, a positive swing of Rs. 139 crore
items.quote: Now coming to the underwriting result for the quarter was Rs. 99 crore compared to a loss of Rs. 40 crore in Quarter 2 of last financial year. This is a positive swing of about Rs. 139 crore.

items.statement: H1 FY27 underwriting result Rs. 210 crore vs loss of Rs. 24 crore in H1 FY26, surpassing full-year FY26 underwriting result of Rs. 198 crore
items.quote: For H1 FY27, our underwriting results stood at Rs. 210 crore as against a loss of Rs. 24 crore in H1 of FY26, giving a positive swing of Rs. 234 crore for H1. The underwriting results for H1 FY27 surpassed the full-year FY26 underwriting result of Rs. 198 crore.

items.statement: Combined Insurance Service Ratio improved by 2.9% to 98% in Q2 FY27 and by 2.4% to 97.9% for H1 FY27
items.quote: The Combined Insurance Service Ratio, CISR, improved by 2.9% to 98% in Quarter 2 FY27 and by 2.4% to 97.9% for H1 of FY27.

items.statement: Profit after tax for Q2 increased over threefold to Rs. 265 crore from Rs. 80 crore; H1 PAT increased 57% YoY to Rs. 815 crore
items.quote: The profit after tax for the quarter increased over threefold to Rs. 265 crore from Rs. 80 crore in the last year same quarter. And the PAT for the half year increased by 57% year-on-year to Rs. 815 crore.

items.statement: Normalized PAT for Q2 increased 70% YoY to Rs. 390 crore; H1 normalized PAT increased 56% YoY to Rs. 775 crore with normalized ROE 15.1%
items.quote: Under the normalized framework, our profit after tax for Quarter 2 increased 70% year-on-year to Rs. 390 crore. The profit after tax for H1 increased 56% year-on-year to Rs. 775 crore, with a normalized ROE on annualized basis increasing from 11.2% of last year's H1 FY26 to 15.1% ROE in H1 FY27.

items.statement: Gross written premium on reported 1/n basis increased 19% YoY to Rs. 5,275 crore for Q2 and 19% YoY to Rs. 9,562 crore for H1
items.quote: The gross written premium on reported 1/n basis increased 19% year-on-year to Rs. 5,275 crore for Quarter 2 and also by 19% year-on-year to Rs. 9,562 crore for the H1.

items.statement: Fresh retail health GWP grew 35% YoY for Q2 and 36% YoY for H1 on reported 1/n basis
items.quote: On the reported 1/n basis, the fresh retail health has grown by 35% year-on-year for the quarter and 36% year-on-year for the half year.

items.statement: New-to-insurance mix rose to 93% for Q2 from 89% in Q2 FY26; new-to-insurance policies grew over 10% YoY and average sum insured rose 13% YoY
items.quote: The new-to-insurance mix rose to 93% for the quarter from 89% in Quarter 2 FY26, reflecting our continued focus on first-time buyers of health insurance and selecting a more healthier pool. The growth during the quarter was led by both volume and value, with the number of new-to-insurance policies growing over 10% year-on-year and the average sum insured also rising 13% year-on-year.

items.statement: Retail Health market share stood at 29% for H1 FY27 and 30% for Q2; like-for-like comparability will be restored only by FY28
items.quote: Our Retail Health market share stood at 29% for H1 FY27 and 30% for the quarter. As highlighted earlier, the reported market share continues to be influenced by the share of long-term policies and the consequent 1/n reporting and like-for-like comparability will be restored only by FY28.

items.statement: Estimate new-to-insurance market share closer to 40-odd percent
items.quote: My estimation is that on new-to-insurance, Star Health will have significant market share probably closer to 40-odd percent. I think that is our estimate, but we may be wrong.

items.statement: Proprietary channels (agency and digital D2C) contributed over 90% of retail business; added 39,000 new agents in H1 FY27, taking network to 8.7 lakh agents
items.quote: Our proprietary channels, agency and digital D2C, contributed over 90% of our retail business, giving us greater control over customer selection, quality of sales, and the economics of acquisition. We added 39,000 new agents during H1 FY27, taking our network to 8.7 lakh agents.

items.statement: Agency productivity improved 19% YoY in H1; fresh business growth from semi-urban and rural geographies over 3 times that of metro and urban
items.quote: Our agency productivity improved by 19% year-on-year during H1. The agency continues to deepen penetration where it matters most, with fresh business growth from semi-urban and rural geographies at over 3 times that of metro and urban geographies.

items.statement: D2C channel grew 137% YoY in H1, led by younger customers, higher sum insured, and rising participation from non-metro and tier 2 markets; D2C share in overall fresh business rose from 8% to 13%
items.quote: Our proprietary digital D2C channel remains the fastest growing, with 137% year-on-year growth in H1, led by younger customers, higher sum insured levels, and rising participation from non-metro and tier 2 markets. Our D2C channel continues to have superior combined ratios.

items.statement: More than 50% of active agents utilizing proprietary ATOM Pro platform
items.quote: On the distribution side, ecosystem engagement on our proprietary ATOM Pro platform continued to deepen, with more than 50% of our active agents are utilizing the platform.

items.statement: Retail claim settlement ratio increased over 1% to 92.4% for H1 FY27; renewal ratio improved 4% to 102%; overall NPS improved 4 points to 65 as of September 2026
items.quote: Our retail claim settlement ratio increased by over 1% to 92.4% for H1 FY27. Our renewal ratio improved by 4% to 102%. Overall company-level NPS also improved by 4 points to 65 as of September 2026.

items.statement: Settled 22.5 lakh claims in H1 FY27 with 83% cashless, probably highest in industry
items.quote: We settled 22.5 lakh claims during the first half of this year and 83% of those claims were settled on a cashless mode, which is probably the highest in the industry.

items.statement: Multi-year policies share in fresh book close to 50%; premium earned over contract term providing visibility and stability to earned revenue base
items.quote: On a fresh basis, we are close to 50%.

items.statement: Price hike last cycle covered close to 80% of book; remaining 20% being repriced this year; further corrections based on loss ratio requirements will happen
items.quote: Whatever we had taken in the last cycle, that was close to 80% of the book. So largely we had covered the entire thing, but whatever got left out, we are taking it this year, and we have plans in place for that.

items.statement: Loss cost held to mid-single-digit numbers; earned premiums grown close to double-digit; differential helping improve loss ratio
items.quote: if you were to take a combined effect of frequency and severity, the loss cost is something that we have been able to hold on to mid-single-digit numbers. That is what has helped us manage this number because our earned premiums have grown close to a double-digit number, and the differential is what is helping us improve the loss ratio.

items.statement: Renewal book now operating at less than 100% combined ratio
items.quote: But as far as renewal book on standalone basis is concerned, that is now operating less than 100% combined ratio.

items.statement: Home healthcare and telemedicine served over 1 lakh consultations/services in Q2; helped manage medical frequency of claims below last year Q2 despite increase in surgical frequency
items.quote: For the quarter, we could actually do more than lakh of consultations as well as home care services. That's the number that we already provided. The specific impact on the loss ratio is something that we do not disclose, but that's one of the big contributors in terms of medical frequency of claims coming down. Even though there was an increase in surgical frequency, but overall this helped us to

items.statement: Partnership with Amplify Health live with automation of FWA capabilities; detection of fraud, waste, abuse strengthened across billing, tariff, medical necessity parameters
items.quote: In underwriting and claims, our partnership with Amplify Health has gone live with automation of FWA capabilities. Sharper analytics is increasingly refining our risk selection and claims decision, and our detection of fraud, waste, and abuse has been considerably strengthened across billing, tariff, and medical necessity parameters.

items.statement: AI-driven quality assurance analyzing over 10 million minutes of customer interaction across 9 languages
items.quote: To further refine our digital acquisition strategy, we scaled our AI-driven quality assurance capabilities, analyzing over 10 million minutes of customer interaction across 9 languages.

items.statement: Welcome proposed Public Insurance Registry as digital public infrastructure; can reduce information asymmetry, strengthen underwriting, simplify claims, strengthen fraud detection
items.quote: We welcome the proposed Public Insurance Registry envisaged as a digital public infrastructure for insurance by enabling policyholders, insurers, and other participants to discover, verify, and exchange information in a consistent manner.

items.statement: Support IRDAI consultation paper on Recalibrating Economics of Insurance Distribution; framework aligned with Star Health's distribution model built over 2 decades
items.quote: We welcome the direction of the proposed reforms and support the intent of better outcomes for customers. The framework envisaged in the paper is closely aligned with the distribution model that Star Health has built over 2 decades.

items.statement: Over 90% retail business from proprietary channels; individual agents better rewarded under proposed framework; engaging agents to sustain earnings through higher productivity
items.quote: Our core business model is very resilient, with over 90% of our retail business being sourced through proprietary channels. Individual agents remain the better rewarded distributors under the proposed framework, and we are engaging closely with our agents to sustain and enhance their earnings through higher productivity.

items.statement: Internal estimates indicate credible path to proposed expense of management limits via prudent management, operating leverage, productivity enhancements through digitization and automation
items.quote: Our internal estimates indicate a credible path to the proposed expense of management limits as a combination of prudent management, operating leverage, and productivity enhancements through our digitization and automation initiatives.

items.statement: Cognizant of authority's focus on dark patterns in digital journeys; will ensure full alignment with evolving framework; consent-led data collection, transparent access, clear disclosures will reinforce trusted direct brands
items.quote: We are cognizant of the authority's sharp focus on dark patterns in digital journeys and we fully share the emphasis on consumer trust. As digital channels account for a growing share of how consumers buy and service their policies, we continue to review our digital journeys and will ensure full alignment with the evolving framework.

items.statement: Equity allocation currently slightly less than 14%; internal strategy caps at 15% max; may increase if markets extremely attractively priced
items.quote: Currently, our equity allocation is 14%. We have decided that it would be max up to 15%, and beyond 15%, we would take a call if markets are extremely attractively priced.

items.statement: Increased portfolio duration given G-Sec yields shot up; desire to be around 4 years duration; currently there, may look at longer duration if yields continue to increase
items.quote: Secondly, in terms of your question regarding duration, yes, we have increased the duration of the portfolio given the fact that G-Sec yields have substantially shot up. We have taken some long-duration assets in the portfolio. Our desire is to be somewhere around 4 years duration for the portfolio.

items.statement: REITs and InVITs fully invested at regulatory limit of 3%; AIF book growing at approximately 2.1-2.2% of funds deployed
items.quote: As far as REITs and InvITs are concerned, regulatory limit is 3%, and we are more or less fully invested with some margin of safety there. AIF book is something which is growing. So currently approximately 2.1% or 2.2% of the funds are deployed in AIFs.

items.statement: Supreme Court order on drug pricing not notified yet; will take time to execute; generally reflects in itemized bills not package pricing; overall surgical claims inflation has been going up
items.quote: The Supreme Court order is not notified yet, and it will take its own time for it to get executed. Generally, these things do not directly impact the package pricing that we have negotiated with the hospitals. It generally reflects in the itemized bills that happens just on the medical admissions. But we will have to see how this develops. We have seen earlier that there was caps on stent pricing

items.statement: Awaiting clarifications on whether second and third year commissions for multi-year policies will be considered fresh or renewal under distribution regulations
items.quote: On your question on regulations for the second and third year, we are awaiting clarifications. We have sought clarification whether second and third year will be considered as fresh or renewal for the purpose of distribution regulations. We are awaiting clarifications.

items.statement: AUM growth guidance of 30-35% for FY27 and similar expectation for FY28
items.quote: already I have given in the previous call also this year's guidance is around 30% to 35%. We have already achieved 20% in the first half. But all the season that is basically Navratri and Diwali is coming in the second half of the year. So, comfortably we will reach our 30% to 35% of growth '27. And similarly, we are expecting for the '28.

items.statement: Preferential issue of ~INR100 crore approved, funds expected by 6th November to boost capital adequacy
items.quote: we are successfully raising approximately INR100 crores through a preferential issue, further strengthening our capital base and providing additional headroom to support a future loan book expansion.

items.statement: Capital adequacy ratio at 24.69% pre-fund raise; expected to support 4-6 quarters of growth post infusion
items.quote: our capital adequacy ratio remained healthy at 24.69%, well above the regulatory requirement, providing ample headroom to support future growth.

items.statement: INR600 crore of borrowings at old higher rates to be repaid by March 2027, reducing cost of funds
items.quote: almost INR600 crores of my total borrowing is lying in the old sanction rates, which will drive down by 31st of March, okay? So that will affect -- that will give a lot of impact on my finance cost.

items.statement: Cost of borrowing expected to fall ~25 bps in Q3-Q4 FY27 due to rating upgrade and repricing
items.quote: overall impact will come 25 bps in the third to fourth quarter.

items.statement: Incremental borrowing cost already 50 bps lower since September due to rating upgrade
items.quote: currently, we are raising a fund at around 50 basis points lower than what we were raising since September.

items.statement: October disbursements already INR120 crore net of rundown; similar expected in November
items.quote: October has already started showing -- we are adding only in the month of October, INR120 crores new AUM after running down the October -- rundown of October also. And equally the same we are expecting in the month of November also.

items.statement: 2-wheeler 83.1%, top-up 5.7%, 3-wheeler 3%, used vehicle 1.6%; over 95% portfolio secured
items.quote: Talking about the product mix for the period under review, 2-wheeler accounted for 83.10 percentage, top-up loan 5.70 percentage, 3-wheeler 3 percentage and used vehicle loan 1.60%. This clearly demonstrates that over 95% of our portfolio remains secured.

items.statement: Used 2-wheeler yield 27-28% IRR; top-up/personal loan ~32% IRR; small business loan/MSME LAP 27-28% IRR
items.quote: used 2-wheeler loan at various locations, almost added 100-plus dealers in last 6 months. And of course, the yield is 27 to 28 IRR with a good processing fee and less payout will definitely add and a nice good yield.

items.statement: GNPA 2.96%, NNPA 2.19%; Stage 1 94.4%, Stage 2 2.6%, Stage 3 2.96%; ECL provision INR23 cr vs INR13 cr required
items.quote: As at the end of the quarter, GNPA and NNPA improved substantially to 2.96% and 2.19%, respectively, reflecting a lower delinquency driven by the disciplined underwriting and the strong collection efficiency.

items.statement: New-to-credit borrowers ~40% of book with 75% LTV cap; delinquency similar to overall portfolio
items.quote: NTC share is around 40% in the total book, okay? As far as the comparison is concerned, how they are behaving, it is almost, I can say, similar because we restrict 75% of LTV to the new to credit customers.

items.statement: Bounce rate 18-20%; 7-8% customers remain in bounce across tenure
items.quote: generally, our bounce rate is 18% to 20%. So, this keeps on revolving because once the customer will bounce, then next time he pays also. So, on an average, there are 7% to 8% customers are there who remain bounce across the tenure.

items.statement: Technology spend ~INR2 crore/year; 28-person tech team; disbursement TAT cut from 3.5-4 days to 1.5-2 days, targeting same-day
items.quote: on an average yearly, we spend around INR2 crores on the technology. And this is what -- because what we understood that NBFC, the speed and innovation is the essence of success.

items.statement: Added 16 offices in last year; 100+ dealers onboarded in Karnataka in 60 days; 5-6 new SBL branches added/planned
items.quote: We have added almost 16 offices in this last 1 year. And this office has been added because of the new volumes and new growth.

items.statement: 7 BC partners active, 3 in due diligence; targeting 10-12 live BC partners
items.quote: we have activated BC partner so far, 7 BC partners and 3 BC partners are in discussion and due diligence is going on. So, we have active live 10 to 12 BC partners that will also add to our disbursement.

items.statement: Added 32,330 new customers in Q2; live customer base >2.45 lakh
items.quote: During the quarter, we also added around 32,330 new customers, taking our total live customer base to over 2.45 lakhs.

items.statement: Market share ~15% in locations with 4+ years operations
items.quote: wherever we are there in any location and if we have completed 4 years of operations, then generally, our market share is around 15%.

items.statement: Key 2-wheeler competitors: IDFC, L&T Finance, regional player Berar Finance
items.quote: There are a couple of competitors -- two-wheeler loans, basically IDFC, L&T and there are some regional players, Berar is there. Those are the major players in the competition of the two-wheeler loan.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded to A- stable from BBB+ positive by CARE Ratings
items.quote: I'm happy to share that recently, company's credit rating has been upgraded to A minus stable from BBB plus positive by CARE ratings.

items.statement: Declared second interim dividend of INR0.25 per share (FV INR10) for FY27
items.quote: the company declared second interim dividend of INR0.25 per equity share on a face value of INR10 each for the financial year '26-'27, reflecting our continued commitment towards shareholder value creation.

items.statement: Chairperson changed from Mr. N.R. Parameshwaran to Mrs. Neelam Tater (Independent Director)
items.quote: I would like to highlight the change in the Chairperson of the company from Mr. Nalliepily Ramaswami Parameshwaran to Mrs. Neelam Tater, Independent Directors.

items.statement: Battery replacement financing for EV 3-wheelers launched 2 months ago; pilot for own customers only; 18-month test before scaling
items.quote: we have introduced this product to support our own AUM, which we have blended in 3-wheeler electric rickshas. So today, introduced 2 months back only, and we are focusing only for our own customers only because we want to understand how it runs.

items.statement: Net interest income Q2: INR52 cr (+40% YoY); H1: INR94 cr (+39% YoY); PAT Q2: INR14 cr (+20% YoY); H1: INR27 cr (+28% YoY)
items.quote: For the quarter under review, net interest income stood at INR52 crores, registering a significant growth of 40% year-on-year. And profit after tax for the quarter increased by 20% year-on-year to INR14 crores.

items.statement: Acquired Vimprotech and TIPS for equity value of INR142 crores via slump sales into wholly owned subsidiaries
items.quote: The most important development this quarter is our agreement to acquire 100% of the business of Vimprotech and TIPS for an equity value of INR142 crores.

items.statement: Vimprotech and TIPS reported FY26 revenue of INR61.7 crores at 28% EBITDA margin with 44% CAGR over last three years
items.quote: Together with a robust customer base of 200-plus, they have reported FY26 revenue at INR61.7 crores at an EBITDA margin of 28%, with revenue growing up to 44% CAGR over the last three years.

items.statement: FY27 revenue guidance of INR918-920 crores, 50% EBITDA margin, and PAT around INR90 crores
items.quote: So, this is this is something that we have actually shared with our investors, which is INR918 crores, INR920 crores of top line, and again a 50% EBITDA to that, and a PAT margin, which is -- and a PAT of around INR90 crores.

items.statement: PAT growth guidance of 60-80% for FY27 versus 40-44% implied by INR90 crore target
items.quote: So, we will be able to do much better than and in my previous media interviews also I said that we will not grow our PAT by 40%, but by 60% to 80%.

items.statement: FY27 capex guidance of INR450 crores, with INR213 crores spent in H1 FY27
items.quote: If you look at it, so this quarter, we have done a capex of INR213 crores as compared to INR201 crores last year H1. But the growth has been 21%. So, you can see that we have put in the same amount of capital, but we have grown by 21%. So, you are absolutely on dot that overall, this year, we will be having a capex of INR450 crores, and near to that we are looking at our EBITDA

items.statement: Added 417,000 net pallets in Q2 FY27, targeting 900,000-1.2 million net additions for FY27
items.quote: We have put in round about 417,000 net allot of our pallets. So, the people who are asking this question of whether there is growth since you have 90% of the market, that also comes to rest.

items.statement: Pallet utilization at 89.3%, container utilization at 73.7%, MHE utilization at 82.3% in H1 FY27; targeting 90-91% pallet utilization
items.quote: Pallet utilization stood at 89.3% in line with Q2 FY26. Container utilization was at 73.7%, up from 71.7%. And MHE utilization at 82.3%. As I mentioned on our call last year, we aim to take the pallet utilization to 90%, 91% range over the coming quarters.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin at 50.8%, up 91 bps YoY; H1 FY27 EBITDA margin at 52.1%
items.quote: With respect to EBITDA was INR1,097 million, up 25%, with EBITDA margin at 50.8%, up 91 basis points year-on-year, supported by higher income, cost optimization, and network synergies.

items.statement: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 22.5% YoY to INR216 crores; H1 FY27 revenue grew 26% YoY to INR429.4 crores
items.quote: So, as compared to last year's quarter 2, we have done INR216 crores of turnover. We have grown by 22.5%.

items.statement: Added 37 new customers in Q2 FY27 (24 LEAP, 13 TARON); 85 new customers in H1 FY27
items.quote: We have added 37 new customers. LEAP has added 24 new customers, and TARON has added 13 new customers. So, overall, in the first half, we have added 85 new customers.

items.statement: Revenue mix: 64% pallets, 20-22% automotive crates/containers, 14-16% MHE
items.quote: So, technically, it is again 64% contribution from pallet side, round about 20-odd percent, 20% to 22% contribution from auto side, and 14% to 16% contribution from MHE side.

items.statement: Plastic granule costs up 30-50%, limiting automotive crate additions; timber costs controlled within 2-3% fluctuation via Plinova
items.quote: But you can look at it that this time the granule cost has gone overboard, plastic cost has gone overboard. Automotive sector has done fantastically well. If they have asked for four crates, we have been able to deliver only 1.5 crates to them.

items.statement: DSO improved from 128 to 122 days; targeting below 90 days by end of FY27 via SAP S/4HANA and centralized POs
items.quote: But as I told you that we have implemented SAP S/4HANA, and the bills are going on time, and you can see that whatever we have billed, we have started collecting more than that. So, we are very confident as a team that by the end of the year, we will be less than 90 days.

items.statement: Post-IPO debt/equity at 0.48x, net debt/EBITDA at 1.9x vs 4.4x in H1 FY26; INR3,596 million debt repaid from IPO proceeds
items.quote: On a post-IPO basis, debt to equity is about 0.48x and net debt to EBITDA is about 1.9x, compared with 4.4x in H1 FY26.

items.statement: India Ratings upgraded long-term rating to A+ from A for both LEAP and TARON; third upgrade in 3.5 years
items.quote: I am very happy to announce that in the month of October, India Ratings and Research, a Fitch Group company, upgraded LEAP's long-term rating from A to A plus, and same has happened for TARON business, which is our MHE business, that has also moved from A to A plus.

items.statement: GCC subsidiaries in Saudi Arabia and UAE established with licenses; engaging 26 customers; targeting revenue from next quarter
items.quote: We have got all the approvals, and we have been putting our ground infrastructure right from setting of an entity, getting all licenses, getting warehouse infrastructure, and hiring key people, customer engagement, and regulatory approvals also.

items.statement: Spent INR2.5-3 crores on GCC setup; evaluating acquisitions before full launch; will start pricing if no acquisition materializes
items.quote: We have just spent hardly INR2.5 crores, INR3 crores into the entire licensing and taking up of the office and putting our people out there and meeting the customer. So, we are treading this very cautiously, but in my future times to come, there will be a lot of good news from the GCC market.

items.statement: Movement hire at 720,000 pallets in Q2 FY27; targeting 3.6-3.7 million for FY27 with Q4 expected at ~1 million
items.quote: We have done 720,000 transfer hire movements in this quarter. And going forward, I believe that the situation will get corrected, and we will be able to hit our numbers of 3.6 million transfer hire movement for this year.

items.statement: Per pallet yield increased to INR1.54/day (INR562-565/year) from INR1.46-1.48; targeting INR1.62 with 3.6M movements
items.quote: If you look at our previous per pallet yield, it was INR1.46, 1.48 paise. Now it has jumped to INR1.54 paise. So, if you look at INR1.54 paise, you multiply by 365 days, we generate round about INR562 to INR565 per annum with a 50% EBITDA, yes.

items.statement: Other income comprises LEC (lost equipment charge) and BBR (broken beyond economic repair) recoveries; 0.5-1.25% of pool goes through this annually
items.quote: This comprises of something which is known as LEC, lost equipment charge. If a customer loses the equipment, they have to pay entire INR1,750 to us. Then the BBR, broken beyond economic repair.

items.statement: Converting customers from static to movement hire in dairy, textile, bottles; 60 companies in sales funnel for transfer hire
items.quote: We have round about 60 companies that we are talking to as far as transfer hire movements are concerned. And we actually follow it on the basis of the sales funnel.

items.statement: Vimprotech has two production lines covering 50% of crate needs; targeting 100% in-house production over time
items.quote: So, currently, it will be 50-50. Currently, they have two lines. Two lines can only take up 50%. Once we see their productivity and the kind of mix that they take out, and we check the strength and all those stuffs. On the basis of that, over a period of time, we will continue to improve. And over a period of time, 100% of our production will be in-house.

items.statement: Textile industry operating at 20% capacity due to granule costs; plastic goods industry hit by granule rate fluctuation
items.quote: We were looking at 10 times growth in textile, but the textile industry is only not functioning. They are functioning at 20% of their overall production capacity. So, textile industry is not doing well because of the cost of the granules. Plastic good industry is also absolutely hit due to the granule rate fluctuation.

items.statement: Carbon credit market potential in India within 1-2 years could directly boost PAT; already tradeable in GCC
items.quote: am very confident government is working towards it, and if it comes in next one to two years, all this people will buy carbon LEAP India Limited. October 27, 2026 credits from us, and all this will go directly into our PAT, which will be which will be a different ballgame altogether, because we have learned this when we have gone to GCC, because in GCC, you can actually buy and sell carbon credit

items.statement: Aims to maintain EBITDA margin around 30% plus or minus 2 percentage points
items.quote: Going forward, we aim to maintain an EBITDA margin of approximately 30%, plus or minus 2 percentage points, supported by disciplined procurement, manufacturing efficiency and appropriate pricing.

items.statement: Machinery worth Rs 50 million commissioned and orders placed for additional Rs 300 million
items.quote: Machinery worth Rs. 50 million has been purchased and commissioned, and orders have been placed for additional machinery worth approximately Rs. 300 million.

items.statement: Pithampur machining and assembly capacity to double from 900,000 to 1,800,000 units by Q4 FY27; Dewas forging capacity to rise from 3,000 to 5,500 tonnes by Q1 FY28
items.quote: At the Pithampur plant, we plan to increase annual machining and assembly capacity from 900,000 units to 1,800,000 units. Most of the additional capacity is expected to become operational in Q4 FY27. At Dewas, annual forging capacity is planned to increase from 3,000 tonnes to 5,500 tonnes, with the additional capacity expected to become operational in Q1 FY28.

items.statement: Order book approximately Rs 68-70 crore, 78% export and 22% domestic
items.quote: The current order book is approximately Rs. 68 – 70 crore, of which around 78% is export orders and 22% is domestic orders.

items.statement: Finished propeller shafts generate margins 5-10% higher than components
items.quote: Finished propeller shafts generate higher margins because they include additional value addition. Margins on finished shafts can be approximately 5% – 10% higher than on components.

items.statement: Revenue split approximately 64-65% components, balance finished propeller shaft assemblies; mix expected to remain similar
items.quote: Approximately 64% – 65% of the business comes from components , with the balance from propeller-shaft 8 Adroit Industries (India) Limited 28 October 2026 assemblies. We expect the mix to remain broadly similar, with a variation of around five percentage points

items.statement: Added approximately 13 new customers in the quarter; 87.4% of product sales from repeat customers
items.quote: We made progress in expanding our customer base during the quarter, adding approximately 13 new customers. At the same time, 87.4% of our product sales came from repeat customers, reflecting the strength of our established relationships.

items.statement: US subsidiary targeting 200 new customers over next two to three quarters
items.quote: Our goal is to add 200 new customers over the next two to three

items.statement: H1 FY27 exports 82.36% of revenue; US 59.56% of export sales
items.quote: In H1 FY27, exports represented approximately 82.36% of revenue, with the United States accounting for 59.56% of export sales.

items.statement: Believes growth to Rs 250 crore revenue can be managed without additional fundraising
items.quote: I believe we should be able to manage the growth without raising additional funds.

items.statement: Revenue grew 25% QoQ to Rs 426.73 million in Q2 FY27; EBITDA up 13% QoQ to Rs 119.56 million; PAT up 14% QoQ to Rs 85.47 million
items.quote: In Q2 FY27, revenue increased 25% sequentially to Rs. 426.73 million, supported by new customer additions and entry into new segments. EBITDA increased 13% QoQ to Rs. 119.56 million, while profit after tax increased 14% sequentially to Rs. 85.47 million.

items.statement: Sees opportunities from Make in India initiative as customers seek domestically manufactured alternatives for critical shafts currently imported
items.quote: A number of critical shafts are still imported into India. We see opportunities arising from the Make in India initiative as customers look for domestically manufactured alternatives.

items.statement: Global competitors include Dana Spicer, Cummins/Arvin Meritor and Neapco; exports to over 35 countries
items.quote: At the global level, competitors include Dana Spicer, Cummins/Arvin Meritor and Neapco. We export to more than 35 countries and are looking to expand into additional markets.

items.statement: Local inventory in US and Canada enables margins 1.5 to 1.7 times previous levels
items.quote: With local teams and inventory, products can be sold at substantially higher margins than when shipped directly, potentially 1.5 to 1.7 times the previous margin level.

items.statement: Procures tubing and universal joints; tubing will continue to be procured, working to manufacture universal joints in-house by end of November 2026
items.quote: The Company currently procures tubing and universal joints. Tubing will continue to be procured, while the Company is working to obtain the technology to manufacture universal joints in-house. Management's target was to complete this by the end of November 2026, which would further improve margins in the propeller-shaft business.
